Subject: APAC edge slab + US/EU capacity tilt proposal for Nimbus expansion

Hi Sylvia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Nimbus expects a primary traffic surge in APAC for the Q3 pilot (user-facing inference, PII flows restricted to region). You mentioned a soft target of ~220 QPS peak, with sustained 40–60 QPS outside peak windows.

To move fast on the SOW and pricing, we need a regional capacity plan that balances the following:
- APAC: small low-latency edge slab for regulatory/data-residency workloads + burst to regional pool
- EU/US: temporary tilt so APAC can be fronted without adding full permanent nodes immediately

Attached: nimbus_expected_qps.csv (your exported traffic sketch) and an initial_sow_outline.pdf.

Can you confirm:
1) Target date for pilot activation (you mentioned late July?)
2) Any hard data residency zones inside APAC (SG only, or also Tokyo/HK)?
3) Procurement owner + expected PO lead time

If you confirm dates today we can provide a concrete node-level ask (instance types, burst buckets, estimated monthly commit) and a MAP link for signatures.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the recap. Quick answers:
- Pilot activation: target week of 2027-07-26 (engineering deadline).
- Data residency: Singapore only for pilot; long-term may include Tokyo but not in phase 1.
- Procurement owner: procurement@nimbushealth.com; PO turnaround historically 2–3 weeks after SOW sign.

We're comfortable with a small APAC slab for latency-sensitive calls plus routing to EU as fallback. Procurement asked me to attach a short checklist of required contract/controls items (procurement_requirements.docx).

Sylvia
Platform Lead, Nimbus Health

Team — ran the numbers against Nimbus's QPS sketch. High-level proposal:

Proposal (pilot, 8-week window):
- APAC edge slab (Singapore): equivalent of 4x A100-80GB sustained with a burst pool to add ~40% headroom. This covers ~200–250 peak QPS with 20–30ms p95 target for inference-only endpoints.
- EU: no net new permanent capacity for pilot; shift ~20% of spare EU capacity to front APAC fallback for non-residency routes.
- US: absorb remaining traffic; recommend temporary priority deprioritization (tilt) during APAC business hours to preserve cost.

Estimated commit: a 2-month reserved tranche for the APAC slab + burst (converted to monthly equivalent in the attached capacity_model_v1.xlsx). Rough delta to Nimbus monthly OPEX: ~+15–22% depending on burst consumption.

Risks/notes:
- If Nimbus needs Tokyo in phase 1 the slab jumps 1.5x cost.
- SOC2 evidence and network peering lead times can add 2 weeks.

Action items:
- Dylan: confirm pilot activation week (Sylvia confirmed 2027-07-26).
- Mina/Infra: run a quick perf sim on mixed long/short prompts (I attached the model).
- Irene: map compliance checklist items to private deployment controls.

Rishi
Head of Capacity Planning

Attachments: capacity_model_v1.xlsx
